articles.headline: Micron warns memory supply will stay tight as AI demand drives prices higher
articles.summary: Micron said AI demand is keeping memory supply constrained and expects conditions to remain tight through 2027 and 2028. For businesses, this points to higher costs and longer lead times for servers, AI infrastructure, and other memory-dependent purchases, which can affect budgeting and deployment timelines.

articles.headline: US moves to block Chinese data center gear in national security systems
articles.summary: US lawmakers introduced a bill to bar federal agencies from buying certain Chinese optical transceivers used in AI networks. This increases compliance and sourcing risk for firms that sell into government or critical infrastructure markets, while also signaling wider supply-chain scrutiny for networking hardware.

articles.headline: Top AI companies back new self-policing controls for frontier systems
articles.summary: Major AI firms agreed to stronger internal controls, external audits, and board-level oversight for frontier models. Businesses using or buying advanced AI should expect tighter governance expectations, more emphasis on safety controls, and possible knock-on effects for enterprise procurement and compliance.
